headline: The US Army’s Special Forces have graduated their first ten robotics specialists, a new job meant to help units use drones and ground robots.
score_reason: Pool score kept: official, confirmed, but a small first group and a pilot so far.
importance_line: A new kind of Army specialist will advise commanders on drones, ground robots and electronic warfare, which affects soldiers in the field and the Army’s plans to scale the job; for now only ten people in one pilot have finished it.
summary: DefenseScoop reports that ten warrant officers (senior technical specialists) finished a 19-week Robotics Technician Integrator course at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, on Friday, the first group in a new Army job that grew out of a Special Forces pilot. The graduates are meant to advise commanders on using drones, ground robots and electronic warfare tools, and acting Army chief of staff Gen. Christopher LaNeve said in a press release, "We are scaling this across the Army," though for now the pilot stays within Special Forces.
notes: Full article read. The quoted words are from Gen. Christopher LaNeve, acting Army chief of staff, via a press release.
